newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia hints at reprisals if Czechs join NATO.
newsitem.headline: Russia hints at reprisals if Czechs join NATO.

text.p: Moscow's ambassador to Prague warned the Czech Republic on Sunday that key bilateral agreements with Russia might be jeopardised if it joined NATO.
Nikolai Ryabov said the former Warsaw Pact member's entry into the western defence alliance could mean a damaging loss of arms markets for Moscow.
"It would be a real blow for the Russian economy," he told Russia's NTV commercial television.
The ambassador went on to hint that Moscow could reconsider economic deals with Prague if it went ahead.

"Agreements fundamental to the Czech Republic, such as gas deliveries and nuclear energy, create a basis for future problems that our countries would face (if Prague joined NATO)," said Ryabov, former head of Russia's central electoral commission.
NATO plans to issue invitations to some former East Bloc states in July. The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland head the list of prospective members.

Russian officials have stepped up their rhetoric against the expansion plans, which they say threaten Russia's security, in the run-up to a summit between President Boris Yeltsin and U.S. Bill Clinton in Helsinki later this week.

Moscow does not expect to be able to stop the expansion but hopes to use the issue as a lever with which to win concessions from the U.S.-led alliance on arms control agreements and other security and economic issues.
